messages:
prod_incident_bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: high GPU queue on pool 'orion-prod' (queue=11.8k, avg_latency=22s). Autoscaler attempts=5, last_error=ProvisioningTimeout. Paging oncall.
Rachel_Oncall: oncall ack. looking now. what region/pool heatmap?
Carla_Infra: affected AZs: us-west-2a/b. Cloud reports instances provisioning then failing health checks. Autoscaler logs show repeated ProvisioningTimeout and occasional QuotaExceeded when retries hit limits.
Pete_Runtime: runtime metrics show burst of CUDA Xid 31 and Xid 43 across flapping nodes; dmesg shows oom-killer and GPU driver stack traces. Suspect driver memory leak or workload pattern (long sequences) causing kernel OOM.
Nina_Support: receiving high-priority tickets: customers report 504s and long tail latencies. Marking impacted accounts and informing AEs.
Rachel_Oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) shift non-SLA traffic to 'orion-cpu-fallback' 2) reduce per-pod concurrency and disable prefetching 3) cordon nodes that show Xid events 4) try nodegroup with older driver.
Pete_Runtime: rolling runtime config change to disable request prefetch and to cap KV cache to 8GB on this pool. Pushing config now.
Carla_Infra: cordoning flaky nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-orion-7 gpu-orion-8 gpu-orion-15 gpu-orion-16` and draining gracefully. Hooking provider console to warm standby nodegroup with driver 510 image.
Carla_Infra: manual scale request started for 10 instances in fallback nodegroup. provider returned QuotaAvailable but autoscaler backoff prevented automated retry.
prod_incident_bot: ACTIONS: cordon/drain by carla_infra; runtime-config-patch by pete_runtime; routing-change applied (40% fallback)
Pete_Runtime: stack trace sample: ```
E GPU: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1): 31, PID=2214, GPU=1, name=python
E kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 2214 (python) total-vm:3xxxxxxxk
```
Rachel_Oncall: Pete, can you validate whether Xid 31 maps to driver bug or to eager memory spikes? any CUDNN traces?
Pete_Runtime: initial correlation: memory spikes on large-batched requests + a small regression in driver 522. Rolling back new node image to driver 520 for new nodes. Also toggled early_oom in runtime agent to preempt allocations.
Nina_Support: posted preliminary customer advisory: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/4412346999 — concise note with ETA 45m for initial recovery.
Tom_Sales: informing top enterprise POCs verbally now. Asking for any temporary routing to guarantee priority lanes for paying customers.
Rachel_Oncall: enabled priority routing: VIP customers pinned to stable nodegroup where possible. Also added temporary throttling for background jobs.
Carla_Infra: provider says old images (driver 520) are limited in some zones; doing cross-AZ redistribution. Launching replacement nodegroup with driver 520.
prod_incident_bot: MONITOR: queue=11800 -> 5600 (10m) -> 2600 (25m), avg_wait 22s -> 9s. autoscaler_backoff=120s.
Pete_Runtime: after switching newly provisioned nodes to driver 520, Xid events dropped by ~80% on canary nodes. Remaining nodes still show sporadic OOM on very long sequences.
Rachel_Oncall: additional mitigations: 1) enforced max_sequence_length=4096 for orion-prod 2) dropped queue items >60s age for non-VIP 3) increased token-throttling for batch endpoints.
Nina_Support: updating impacted tickets with incident tag 4412346999 and offering credits/priority requeue for affected workloads.
Tom_Sales: collecting list of VIP jobs that need manual reroute. will share doc.
Pete_Runtime: added runtime guard: `gpu_mem_limit_mb=28672` and `enable_early_oom=true`. patch applied to pool.
Carla_Infra: all manual replacements in progress; 12 nodes in new nodegroup provisioning. Provider support ticket opened: CLOUD-100112, request escalation on driver regression.
Rachel_Oncall: monitoring logs and customer impact. queue now ~2.6k stable. preparing to handoff to pete_runtime for overnight monitoring at 23:30 UTC. pete, accept?
Pete_Runtime: accepting handoff. I'll watch for Xid recurrences, validate canary stability, and coordinate with infra for further rollbacks if needed.
prod_incident_bot: HANDOFF: from rachel_oncall -> pete_runtime at 4412347450 (state=mitigated-degraded)
Nina_Support: publishing second customer update: "Mitigations in place; partial recovery observed. Engineering is provisioning stable capacity. We expect normalized service within 2 hours."
